title: Similar forms from divergent genomes point to generic laws of morphogenesis

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Similar forms from divergent genomes point to generic laws of morphogenesis

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Because Anthrobots and Xenobots, despite highly divergent genomes, ages and tissue origins, assemble into very similar kinds of motile constructs, the authors conclude that generic laws of morphogenesis matter in addition to species-specific genomic information.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Gumuskaya G 2024, Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells › Discussion

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Despite their highly divergent genome, age, and tissue origin, the two platforms assemble into very similar types of creatures, illustrating the importance of generic laws of morphogenesis[ 31 ] in addition to species‐specific genomic information.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Gumuskaya G, Srivastava P, Cooper BG, Lesser H, Semegran B, Garnier S, Levin M, “Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells”, Advanced science (Weinheim, Baden-Wurttemberg, Germany) (2024), doi:10.1002/advs.202303575; section “Discussion”. Scope: Self-assembling multicellular constructs from human and amphibian cells

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2024-anthrobots-24: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.50

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Similarity of the two constructs is measurable with existing reports. The inference that generic laws, rather than convergent culture conditions or selected features, explain it is not uniquely discriminated.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Quantify form and movement similarity across human and frog constructs and test whether substrate-independent physical models predict shared outcomes better than species-specific models.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Generic laws are not specified as competing models.

Two engineered platforms provide weak coverage for a general morphogenesis claim.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data existence: 0.68
operationalizability: 0.5
data adequacy: 0.35
analysis feasibility: 0.62
discriminating power: 0.35

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Human and frog genomes are obviously divergent, and both labs produced motile epithelial spheroids. That pair of facts does not separate a generic morphogenetic law from ordinary shared mechanics of ciliated epithelia. Nothing now public, and no reanalysis of genomes or shapes, would count as a confirmation or a refutation of the extra inference.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Genomic distance between human and Xenopus, and similarity of the two motile spheroids, can both be measured. No outcome distinguishes 'generic laws of morphogenesis matter in addition to the genome' from both epithelia obeying the same packing and cilia mechanics in similar culture conditions.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The statement does not name a law, a prediction or a rival model that existing genomes or shapes could reject.

Morphological similarity of two ciliated spheroids is expected from shared culture physics without a further law.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data adequacy: 0.18
data existence: 0.25
analysis feasibility: 0.3
operationalizability: 0.3
discriminating power: 0.12
